PRACTICES.e: Clears 1 bug each retro. +3 against dependency incidents.
Pushed-through features no longer create bugs.
Shelved features still earn 20% of their reward.
Picking 2+ features lowers the combined Dev target by 3.
+2 on Mitigation. Outages no longer hit you harder.
+3 on Development — but pushing through costs 2 bugs, not 1.
One more feature slot per sprint.

PHASES.lead: Each group picks features up to its capacity, then commits.
note: Scope is a commitment, not a wish list
Every feature you add raises one shared bar. Two features are not two chances — they are one harder roll. This is batch size, and it is the same reason large releases fail more often than small ones.

PHASES.lead: One d20 per group against the combined target. All or nothing.
note: Capability is the modifier, not the die. Groups that bought practices early are not luckier — they shifted the whole distribution. Compare the bonus columns at the end.

PHASES.lead: One card. It hits every group, but not equally.
note: The card does not care what you planned. What decides the outcome is what you built three sprints ago — observability, failover, monitoring. Session 04 called this the non-functional half of the architecture.

PHASES.lead: Built is not shipped. Bugs tax every release roll.
note: Technical debt has an interest rate
Each bug is −1 on this roll and on every roll after it, until someone pays it down. At five bugs nothing ships at all. Nobody decided to stop shipping; it just became arithmetic.

PHASES.lead: The world reacts to the portfolio you have actually built.
note: Defensive work pays late, and all at once
Privacy, failover and monitoring earn almost nothing when you build them. They decide this phase. A backlog ranked purely on customer value never gets to them.

PHASES.lead: +2 Investment Points per group. Spend them on permanent practices.
note: A practice bought in sprint 1 applies to every roll that follows; the same practice bought in the last sprint applies to one. This is the whole argument for investing in the way you work while there is still runway.
